successors.name: Teutonic Order
successors.text: Livonia, Estonia and the Courland coast held by the Brothers: the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order

ledger.x: 1202: Bishop Albert of Riga founds the Livonian Brothers of the Sword.
1206: the Livs of Turaida are beaten and declared converted.
1209: the Order's seat moves to Wenden (Cēsis).
1208-1210: Koknese and the Jersika lands pass under the Order and the bishop.
1211: the struggle for Sakala and Ugandi.
By 1218: southern Estonia is in the Order's hands.
1224: the Brothers establish their headquarters at Fellin.
1224: Tālava is divided between the Archbishopric and the Order.
1227: the Order conquers the Danish north of Estonia.
1227: the fighting for Sakala and Ugandi ends.
1237: the remnants of the Brothers join the Teutonic Order.
1237: the Livonian Brothers of the Sword cease to exist.

wars.name: Livonian Crusade, the Brothers' campaigns
wars.outcome: The Brothers took the Livs of Turaida (1206), Koknese and Jersika's capital (1208-1209), Sakala and Ugandi (1211-1227), Saaremaa (1227) and Courland (1230); they were broken at Saule in 1236 and absorbed by the Teutonic Order in 1237.

wars.name: Wars for Sakala and Ugandi
wars.outcome: Fellin taken in 1211, Sakalian resistance destroyed in 1212; fighting 1208-1227 with a truce 1213-1215; southern Estonia held by 1218 (B1).

wars.name: War between the Brothers and Denmark over northern Estonia
wars.outcome: Valdemar II landed at Lindanise on 15 June 1219 and conquered northern Estonia with Albert's help; the partition was disputed (1222); the Brothers took all Danish territories in 1227; the Teutonic Order returned Harria and Vironia to Denmark at Stensby on 7…

wars.name: Conquest of Saaremaa
wars.outcome: A combined attack by the Brothers, Riga and the Bishop of Riga; the Oeselians accepted Christianity.

wars.name: Battle of Saule
wars.outcome: Defeat on 22 September 1236: the Master Volkwin and 48 to 60 knights killed; the remnants were taken into the Teutonic Order in 1237.

certainty.note: Crusader conquests of tribal lands: no treaty lines on the pages opened; the Danish-Order frontier in Estonia was in dispute (B4) and the Semigallian, Lithuanian and Novgorodian frontiers are approximate.
